newsitem.title: HONG KONG: U.N. urges Britain to watch HK post-1997 rights.
newsitem.headline: U.N. urges Britain to watch HK post-1997 rights.

text.p: The United Nations Human Rights Committee has urged Britain to ensure the human rights situation in Hong Kong is monitored after it hands the territory over to Chinese rule next year.

"The committee urges the United Kingdom...to take all necessary steps to ensure effective and continued application of the provisions of the Covenant in the territory of Hong Kong," the committee said in a report made available to the media by the Hong Kong government on Friday.
Britain, a signatory to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR), which the committee monitors, has been reporting regularly on Hong Kong's human rights situation.
But it is uncertain whether the tradition would be carried beyond July 1, 1997, when Hong Kong, a British colony of over a century and a half, reverts to Chinese rule.
Hong Kong has been guaranteed a high degree of self-rule for the next 50 years under Sino-British treaties, the Joint Declaration, and its mini-constitution, the Basic Law.
Beijing, however, has long argued that it will have no obligation to the committee after the sovereignty transfer as it is not a signatory to the Covenant.

But the committee, which met in late October in Geneva to discuss Hong Kong's human rights situation, said it was only in keeping with the Joint Declaration and Basic Law that China reports on Hong Kong's human rights situation.

"The committee pointed out that the parties to the Joint Declaration have agreed that all provisions of the Covenant as applied to Hong Kong shall remain in force after July 1, 1997," the committee said in its report.
"Human rights treaties devolve with territory, and the states continue to be bound by the obligations under the covenant entered into by the predecessor state," it said.
Hong Kong government solicitor-general Daniel Fung said China and Britain were working at a solution to continue applying the Covenant to Hong Kong.
"There's no reason to be pessimistic on this issue," he told a news conference where the report was released.
Britain has been asked by the United Nations to file a final report on Hong Kong's human rights situation for the period leading up to just before it departs the territory next year.
"Britain has been invited to report on the human rights situation in the territory up till the 30th of June 1997," Fung said.
